official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2024 policy change removed the previous de facto planning ban and put onshore wind on the same general NPPF footing as other energy development.
The 2025 Onshore Wind Taskforce strategy records the NSIP route returning for onshore wind above the stated 100MW threshold from 31 December 2025.
A national need for renewable energy does not automatically override landscape, heritage, amenity or other site-specific planning considerations.
Repowering and life-extension policy support does not amount to automatic planning permission for a specific site.
Community-benefit arrangements are distinct from planning permission and do not by themselves cure planning impacts.
Grid connection availability is a separate evidence stream from land-use planning acceptability.
Taskforce commitments and future reform actions must not be treated as operative legal requirements before implementation.
Wind-policy status does not establish ownership, aviation clearance, grid capacity or final development yield.

core_rules: national need is not automatic permission
policy support does not override site impacts
100MW NSIP threshold must retain effective date
local and NSIP routes remain distinct
strategy action is not operative law until implemented
grid connection is not planning permission
planning permission is not grid connection
repowering support is not automatic consent
wind policy does not establish ownership
wind policy does not prove aviation clearance
wind policy does not prove grid capacity
wind policy does not calculate yield
technical evidence must be site specific
no parcel wind clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
